rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; the model says a married filing separately return must show the spouse's name and SSN (i1040gi p. 14, Married Filing Separately, "Enter your spouse's name in the entry space. The person collection holds the people whose income and items are on the return (f1040 p. 1, "If joint return, spouse's first name and middle initial"). Married filing separately is refused for the whole return (s3.mfs, i1040gi p. 14), so no computed return needs the separate filer's spouse as a name entry.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 14, Test 1: "Your parent didn't have to live with you." The objection is test1_persons' (the helper label read as excluding a parent who lives with you), inherited through the count: Test 1 met is test1_persons above 0, which is the source's "either Test 1 or Test 2 applies" for Test 1. As ruled for test1_persons, the helper dependent.hoh_test1 has no residence condition, and a co-resident parent who fails Test 1 on the label's reading meets Test 2 on the same facts. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 14, Test 1: "You paid over half the cost of keeping up a home that was the main home for all of 2025 of your parent whom you can claim as a dependent ... Your parent didn't have to live with you." The model reads the helper's label ("through a parent who does not live with you (a parent who lives with you qualifies you through Test 2)") as excluding a parent who lives with you. The helper's expression (dependent.hoh_test1: parent, your dependent, dependent.parent_home_paid) has no residence condition, and parent_home_paid asks about "a home that was their main home" without one, so such a parent counts under Test 1. If a filer answered no for that parent because of the label, Test 2 qualifies on the same facts. The label is imprecise but has no wrong effect. Same as the completeness-fixes ruling. Project stands.
